description: Falco is a cloud-native security tool designed for Linux systems. It employs custom rules on kernel events, which are enriched with container and Kubernetes metadata, to provide real-time alerts. Falco helps you gain visibility into abnormal behavior, potential security threats, and compliance violations, contributing to comprehensive runtime security.

panels.title: Rules
panels.description: Rule matches in the selected range, by rule.

panels.title: Sources
panels.description: Rule matches in the selected range, by event source.

panels.title: Priorities
panels.description: Rule matches in the selected range, by Falco priority (exported as 0 emergency to 7 debug).

panels.title: by Priority over time
panels.description: Rule matches per displayed interval (minimum 1 minute), by Falco priority.

panels.title: by Source over time
panels.description: Rule matches per displayed interval (minimum 1 minute), by event source.

panels.title: by Rule over time
panels.description: Rule matches per displayed interval (minimum 1 minute), by rule.

panels.title: Scap events/s by instance
panels.description: Kernel events captured per second by each Falco instance, plus the total. A drop to zero means Falco stopped seeing events.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU used by each Falco container (cAdvisor), as a share of one core: 100% = 1 core. Falco has no CPU limit. falcosecurity_falco_cpu_usage_ratio is not used because it is the average since the process started, not current usage.

panels.title: Scap Drops total
panels.description: Kernel events dropped because Falco could not keep up. Any increase means events, and possibly detections, were missed.

panels.title: Queue Drops
panels.description: Alerts dropped because Falco's output queue was full. Any increase means alerts were lost before delivery.

panels.title: Scap Drops Buffer
panels.description: Events dropped from the kernel ring buffer, by syscall category (clone_fork, execve, connect, open, dir_file, close, proc, other_interest). A sign the node produces more events than Falco consumes. Falco 0.45 counts drops on the exit path only; its dir="enter" series are fixed zeros kept for compatibility, so they are not shown.

panels.title: Scap Drops Auxmap Pool Full
panels.description: Modern eBPF auxiliary-map pool exhaustion drops. Uses the native metric exported by the installed driver; the legacy CPU-drop metric is not available.

panels.title: Scap Drops Full Threadtable
panels.description: Events dropped because Falco's thread table was full; many short-lived processes can cause it.

panels.title: Scap Drops Scratch Map
panels.description: With the modern eBPF driver this counts events dropped because they exceeded the maximum event size (n_drops_max_event_size).
